newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovaks say need to import 300,000 tonnes of grain.
newsitem.headline: Slovaks say need to import 300,000 tonnes of grain.

text.p: Slovakia will need to import some 300,000 tonnes of grain, as results from this year's crop fail to meet forecasts, Minister of Agriculture Peter Baco said on Wednesday.

Baco added that while the harvest still continued in some northern districts, Slovakia would probably need to buy some 50,000 tonnes to help to cover the annual consumption and about 250,000 tonnes to bolster state reserves.
"According to our preliminary estimates, it seems the grain crop is lower by some 150,000 tonnes against last year," Baco told a news conference.

In August, the Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) revised its 1996 grain harvest forecast to 2.64-2.71 million tonnes from a previous estimate of 2.77-2.82 million. This folowed the third grain crop survey this year in mid-August. It said the latest estimate compared with last year's crop of 2.89 million tonnes.
"On the other hand, it appears we will have some 30 percent more bread grain than the country needs," Baco said, adding the shortage in 1996 appeared mainly to be in feed grains.
Baco also told the news conference that he was not responsible for the illegal export of about 200,000 tonnes of grain this year.
The country's supreme control bureau (NKU) recently said some 200,000 tonnes of grain had been exported by several unspecified Slovak firms, on licences illegally provided by ministry officials.
The NKU said the licences were issued after September 12 last year when the state banned further export licences after 1995 grain crop estimates appeared to be incorrect.
"All documents we have so far on this case show that somebody from the Ministry of Economy issued these licences, with no intervention by my ministry," Baco said.
Earlier this week opposition deputies asked for an extraordinary session of parliament to hold a no-confidence vote on Baco.
"The last year's crop estimates were incorrect all around the world, and we have managed this situation succesfully, despite these licences being issued after the prohibition date," Baco said.
